title: Dayshift on-call handoff sketch
content:
Purpose: quick, readable dayshift handoff + temporary procedures. This is a sketch — insert screenshots/links later.

Top-of-shift checklist (take ~5-10m):
- Check PagerDuty for any active incidents (filter: redwood-prod, serving-runtime).
- Open SLO dashboard (Console -> SLOs -> serving-runtime) — note any breaches in last 24h.
- Verify alert inbox: errors@redwood and #oncall-ops Slack.
- Confirm CI deploys: glance at last 3 deploys for failed jobs (ci.redwood/dev).
- Local quick sanity: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .status -> expect "ok"

Shift summary template (fill at handoff):
- Ongoing items: short bullets of anything that needs follow-up.
- Known degradations + workaround: e.g., embedding-queue throttled, use low-priority route.
- Recent escalations: who was paged, ticket ids, outcome.
- Commands run and why: brief audit so next person can replicate.

Quick troubleshooting snippets
- Check runtime instance health (k8s): kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=inference -o wide
- Restart a failing runtime pod: kubectl -n serving rollout restart deploy/inference-runtime
- Inspect CPU/GPU usage on node: rsh $NODE -- nvidia-smi; top -b -n1 | head
- Check request traces: jaeger UI -> service=inference-runtime -> search for high-latency traces
- Look for cache-miss storm: redis-cli -h cache.prod.redwood keys '*' | grep kvcache (careful, do not run in prod without pattern)

Temporary mitigation recipes (for dayshift, until SRE/ENG can patch):
1) High 95th latency for small requests:
   - Confirm batching queue backlog (metrics: runtime.batch.pending). If backlog > 200, scale up GPU pool (console -> dedicated -> scale) or flip traffic to cheaper pool: PATCH /routes/:id -> route.policy={fallback: true}
   - If scaling not immediate, route low-priority customers to v2-quantized model via quick switch: curl -X POST $ADMIN/switch_model -d '{"route":"/text-gen","model":"gpt-lite-q4"}'
2) Model OOMs on a node:
   - Drain node: kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
   - Remove offending pod image (if repeated) and escalate with tag + logs.
3) Embedding ingestion lag:
   - Temporarily switch embedding jobs to batch window (cron-job: embeddings-batch -> pause: kubectl scale job/embeddings-stream --replicas=0)

Escalation playbook (who to page):
- First tier: oncall-eng (PD group). If no response in 10m -> SRE lead (Jon Rivera).
- Second tier (for infra-level outages): Platform on-call (Priya Desai) -> escalate to Eng Director (Luca Moretti).
- Pager text template: "[SEV?] {brief impact, e.g., Serving runtime 95p latency 2x for prod routes} — seen at {time} — temp mitigation {what you did}. Need {what you need}."

Notes about communication:
- Post an initial incident message in #oncall-ops within 5m with high-level impact + link to traces.
- Keep updates every 15m until resolved.
- After resolution, file a short postmortem stub and tag SRE for follow-up.

Housekeeping items to hand off if unresolved:
- Open tickets to create: change to autoscaler thresholds, add circuit-breaker for route X, tune batching window.
- Ownership: who will take the follow-up? mark in ticket and ping them in Slack.

Known quirks / local TODOs (notes-to-self):
- API health endpoint returns 200 even when kv-cache is hot; consider adding cache-miss metric to /health.
- Debug script for trace export: ~/scripts/export-traces.sh is flaky on laptop; copy to /tmp and run with --since=1h.
- Remember: admin model-switch endpoint requires MFA if done from web console; CLI token can do quick switch. document token rotation.

Unresolved questions (bring to engineering retro):
- Why do certain low-length text-gen requests spike the small-bert embedding service? hypothesis: telemetry/agent causing accidental embedding calls.
- Is there a safe guardrail for batch window reset when memory pressure is high? current autoscaler doesn't account for per-model KV cache.

Handoff checklist (before leaving):
- Fill the Shift summary template above and post in #oncall-handoffs with subject: "Dayshift Handoff {date HH:MM} - {brief}"
- Create or update follow-up tickets, assign owner.
- Confirm next oncall acknowledged (PD ack).
- Leave this doc link in the handoff message.

Quick links (copy into Slack message):
- SLO dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/slo/serving-runtime
- PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com
- Traces/Jaeger: https://traces.redwood.ai
- CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/pipelines
- Runbook index (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Runbooks
Personal notes (scratch):
- If latency is intermittent, try zooming traces by request-id (add ?span=top) to see model switch events.
- Keep an eye on the quantized pool — previous incident (ONCALL-58) happened after a bad autoscale config.

End of sketch. Fill in templates and push to shared runbooks when stable.
summary: Personal dayshift on-call handoff and runbook sketch with checklists, quick commands, temporary mitigations, escalation steps, and handoff template. Draft for personal use before formalizing into shared runbook.
